what: Selection and answer state are keyed by the raw option VALUE string, not by index/id. answers.current[String(slot)]=value (L221), multiSel.has(opt) (L384), pairs.some((p)=>p[1]===v) (L342/342), and React key={opt} (L378,402,416). If served_options contain duplicate display strings, the duplicates collapse into one selectable unit and emit duplicate React keys.
why: Duplicate labels are realistic in matching (the same right-hand category legitimately pairing with two different left terms) and possible in multi_select. When a right value repeats, selecting it for one pair dims BOTH occurrences (rightState L342), so the learner physically cannot complete the required K pairs and is force-timed-out -> a learner who knows the material is misscored/failed. F4 stores VALUE strings (api.ts L7-9) so the server also cannot disambiguate.
suggested_fix: Key options by slot-local index or a stable option id (render key + selection set + pair tuples), submitting the value per the F4 contract but tracking selection by identity so repeated labels remain independent.

what: enterGuest() (the free 'Guest Mode' path) has no try/finally around its awaits. Unlike onLogin/onCreateAccount/onResetPassword which wrap work in try{...}finally{setBusy(false)}, enterGuest sets busy=true then awaits AsyncStorage.getItem('ape:careerfinder:v1'), resetAllLocalStores(), resetAmplitudeOrientation() and AsyncStorage.setItem('ape:localUserId','') unguarded; only supabase.auth.signOut() is in a try/catch.
why: If any of those unguarded calls throw (e.g. a native AsyncStorage/store failure), setBusy(false) at line 150 never runs and toHome() is never reached: the spinner replaces the button stack permanently, no error is shown, and the user cannot enter the app or retry via the primary no-account entry point.
suggested_fix: Wrap the enterGuest body in try/catch/finally: setBusy(false) in finally and setError(...) in catch, matching the other auth handlers.

what: The first-run welcome modal enforces a 9s WELCOME_DELAY_MS before the 'LET'S GET STARTED' button renders (canContinue), but during that window NO wait/countdown affordance is shown: the styles.wait ('PLEASE WAIT') style is defined (lines 88-95) yet never rendered, and onRequestClose only calls dismiss() when canContinue is true, so Android hardware-back silently no-ops for 9 seconds.
why: For 9 seconds the user sees a card with no button, no timer, and an unresponsive back gesture, with nothing on screen indicating a wait is intended -- code-level the overlay presents no progress/disabled-state readout, so it is wired to read as a frozen/hung screen.
suggested_fix: Render the defined styles.wait indicator (or a countdown/disabled button) while !canContinue so the forced dwell is communicated, per the code's own intent.

what: useFocusEffect calls fetchAchievementsHub().then(setHub).catch(() => setHub(null)); a fetch error resets hub to null, which is the exact initial/loading value the render keys off (RecentStrip loading, counts render '— / —'). An error is therefore indistinguishable from loading and the hub sits in a permanent loading skeleton with no retry affordance within the current focus.
why: A transient failure on the Trophy Case hub leaves the three category cards stuck as loading placeholders with '— / —' counts and no message; the user cannot tell the difference between 'still loading' and 'failed', and there is no in-screen retry (only a tab re-focus refetches).
suggested_fix: Track an explicit error flag distinct from null/loading (e.g. setHub({error:true}) or a separate useState), and render an error line with a retry/pull action when fetchAchievementsHub rejects.

what: When fetchNotificationPrefs() returns null on a TRANSIENT network/RLS failure (not just a guest), the whole NOTIFICATIONS body treats the signed-in member as having no session: every Toggle is disabled={!prefs} and the dependency note (line ~330) reads 'Sign in to manage notifications — a guest session keeps nothing.' A paying Academy member with a blip is told they are a guest and can change nothing, with no retry.
why: prefs===null is overloaded to mean both 'no account' and 'fetch failed'; isMember comes from context (still 'academy') so the members-only section renders, but all controls dead-end on the null prefs with a wrong message.
suggested_fix: Distinguish a null-because-guest from a null-because-error (return a discriminated result from fetchNotificationPrefs); on error show a retry affordance and keep the correct member wording.

what: entitlement defaults to 'anonymous' (line ~150) and is only corrected after an async supabase read. During that window a signed-in Academy/free user renders the guest state everywhere: Settings shows MEMBERSHIP 'GUEST — NO ACCOUNT', hides Student ID + Delete Account, shows 'Sign in / create account'; Profile shows statusLabel 'REFERENCE MODE' and the UPGRADE CTA.
why: No pending/loading tier; the derived tier only lands after getSession()+entitlements select resolves, so the first paint of every launch shows a wrong entitlement (self-corrects, but visible).
suggested_fix: Add a 'loading' tier state (or gate entitlement-dependent UI on a resolved flag) so screens render a neutral/loading membership rather than the anonymous ladder rung before the server read completes.

what: The notification-tap handler attachWeeklyConceptPush (plus queueWeeklyConcept / flushWeeklyConceptNav) is defined in push.ts but is never imported or called anywhere in the app — a whole-tree grep finds callers only for registerAndSavePushToken, not for the response listener. No other addNotificationResponseReceivedListener / getLastNotificationResponseAsync exists in the source.
why: registerAndSavePushToken only registers the device token so the server can SEND pushes; nothing ever attaches the tap listener that calls nav(payload) -> WeeklyConcept (and onLocal(dest) for local reminders). So tapping a weekly-concept push or a local reminder never deep-links: it cold-opens the app to Main/Auth. SplashScreen (lines 35-49) is explicitly written to PRESERVE a 'WeeklyConcept'/'Awards' route pushed by a tap, but that route is never pushed because the handler is unwired — making WeeklyConceptScreen effectively unreachable through its sole intended entry point.
suggested_fix: Attach attachWeeklyConceptPush(nav, onLocal) once at app startup (e.g. in RootNavigator/App after the nav container is ready), mapping payload -> navigation.navigate('WeeklyConcept', payload) and dest 'glossary'/'awards' -> their routes; also call flushWeeklyConceptNav on ready to drain any queued cold-start payload.

what: For no_pass and timed_out outcomes the body copy invites the user to retake ('You may retake the Final Exam whenever you are ready'), but the only control on the screen is a single 'Done' button (lines 97-103) that calls navigation.goBack(). Because doSubmit ran navigation.popToTop() before pushing this screen (FinalExamScreen.tsx line 124), the AwardProgress gate that launches the exam is no longer on the stack, so goBack lands on Main, not on a retake entry point.
why: The promised retake path is not reachable from the result screen; the user is dropped to the dashboard and must re-navigate Home/Awards/AwardProgress to start again. Copy and available affordance contradict each other for a core capstone flow.
suggested_fix: Add a 'Retake Final Exam' button on no_pass/timed_out that re-navigates to AwardProgress (or directly re-launches FinalExam with the same awardType/awardId/awardName), instead of only offering Done->Main.

what: The offline submit path (enqueueExamSubmission in FinalExamScreen.tsx lines 127-135; replayExamSubmissions in api.ts) surfaces the replayed capstone result only through Alert.alert in DashboardScreen.tsx lines 695-701. FinalExamScreen's own comment (lines 130-134, B-148) documents that RN-web Alert.alert is a no-op and is why the exam screen switched to notify(); DashboardScreen still uses raw Alert.alert for the replay.
why: On the web preview an offline-submitted Final Exam (a once-per-award capstone) yields NO visible result and NO 'Credential awarded' message, and the FinalExamResult screen is never shown for the offline path at all. The pass/credential outcome is silently lost on web.
suggested_fix: Surface replayed exam results with notify()/confirmDialog (or route to FinalExamResult) rather than Alert.alert, consistent with the fix already applied in FinalExamScreen.

what: User-placed Home topic cards resolve their title via HOME_TOPIC_INDEX (built from the RETIRED v2 MATRIX_SUBJECTS, lines 101-105) then officialTopicName(gs, HOME_TOPIC_INDEX.get(gs)?.name) at lines 1031-1037. Home gs values are v3 topic ids; a v3 gs absent from the v2 matrix falls to officialTopicName(gs, undefined), which only codifies 5 ids (3060/3070/3081/3970/4370) and otherwise returns the literal string 'this topic'. subject is '' and hidden.
why: An academy member who placed a curriculum topic on Home whose gs is not one of the 5 codified names gets a carousel card whose big title reads 'this topic' (and no subject). Violates the Booth 2026-09-03 rule that no placeholder/gs may reach the user, and the card cannot be told apart from any other unresolved card.
suggested_fix: Resolve Home topic names against the LIVE v3 curriculum (fetchV3Curriculum) instead of the v2 MATRIX_SUBJECTS index, or expand OFFICIAL_TOPIC_NAMES to cover every enrollable v3 gs; never render the 'this topic' fallback as a card title.

what: The stranded-session self-heal banner (lines 1375-1401, 'You're signed in, but this account isn't set up for study yet') is dead: setStrandedSession is only ever called with false (init line 906, load() line 930). No code path calls setStrandedSession(true). load() now always builds the public catalog with no user/enrollment query, so the branch that would flag a stranded authed account was removed but the banner UI/state were left behind.
why: A signed-in account with no student record / no enrollment silently drops into the public (free) catalog with NO 'Complete Registration' or 'Sign Out' recovery prompt. The user cannot tell their account is mis-provisioned and has no affordance to fix it or switch accounts.
suggested_fix: Either restore a detection path that calls setStrandedSession(true) when an authed session has no student/enrollment record, or remove the dead state+banner if the product no longer wants it. Do not ship a recovery affordance that can never render.

what: fetchV3Curriculum() (lines 133-149) swallows all errors internally and returns [] on failure. When it returns [] (network/RLS failure OR genuinely empty), v3Subjects stays [], the subject tree (lines 262-324) renders nothing, and the stat tiles show '—'/0 (STUDY TOPICS, SUBJECT CATEGORIES). There is no loading indicator, no error message, and no retry.
why: On a failed curriculum load the entire Explore/Curriculum page reads as an empty reference screen with dashes and a blank tree, indistinguishable from a real 'no data' state, and the user has no way to retry.
suggested_fix: Track a loading/error flag from fetchV3Curriculum (return a discriminated result or expose the caught error) and render a distinct loading spinner, an error message with Retry, and an explicit empty state, instead of silently collapsing to a blank tree.

what: WeeklyConcept is registered as a modal in RootNavigator (line 240) with a full param contract (types.ts lines 102-112), but no navigate('WeeklyConcept') exists anywhere in the audited source. Its only intended entry point is the push-tap handler in src/features/notifications/push.ts (attachWeeklyConceptPush / flushWeeklyConceptNav / queueWeeklyConcept), and grep shows those exports are never imported or called anywhere in appsrc.
why: The weekly misunderstood-concept push notification, when tapped, has no wired code path to open the screen, so the feature is silently dead — the user can never reach WeeklyConcept.
suggested_fix: Attach the push handler at the NavigationContainer root (e.g. call attachWeeklyConceptPush((payload) => navigationRef.navigate('WeeklyConcept', payload)) and flushWeeklyConceptNav on ready) so a notification tap actually navigates; otherwise remove the dead route and push plumbing.

what: PublicGlossaryScreen (src/screens/landing/PublicGlossaryScreen.tsx) renders GlossaryScreen through a navProxy that remaps navigate('Dashboard') -> goBack(). But GlossaryScreen's header, StudyHeader, calls (navigation).popTo('Dashboard') using its OWN useNavigation() hook (StudyHeader.tsx lines 40 and 70) — it never sees the proxy. In the PublicGlossary (root-level) context there is no 'Dashboard' route in the root stack, so popTo('Dashboard') is unhandled (RN7 emits 'POP_TO was not handled by any navigator') and no-ops.
why: If a user reaches PublicGlossary (currently dev-only, but this is the designed anonymous browse path), the primary header back control (‹ RETURN / method icon) does nothing, stranding them on the glossary. The proxy back-fix only covers the navigate('Dashboard') path, not the header's popTo.
suggested_fix: Have PublicGlossary pass an explicit onBack/return handler that GlossaryScreen/StudyHeader use in public mode (e.g. StudyHeader accepts an optional onBack that defaults to popTo('Dashboard') but is overridden to navigation.goBack() here), or intercept popTo in the navProxy as well.

what: No backward navigation between questions. `advance()` (L209-217) only ever calls setQIdx((i)=>i+1) or doSubmit; qIdx is never decremented and there is no Prev/Back-to-question control. Tap-to-select auto-advances after a 350ms highlight, so a learner cannot return to, review, or change any earlier answer.
why: Owner-priority sequence requirement (question->next AND back) is unmet. A mis-tap is permanent: the answer is recorded to answers.current on selection and the screen jumps forward with no correction path within the single sitting.
suggested_fix: Add a previous-question control (or a review step before final submit) that decrements qIdx and rehydrates picked/multiSel/pairs from answers.current[String(slot)], or explicitly document/confirm that answers are final-on-tap in the UI.

what: Android hardware back is not intercepted. The only guarded exit is the header chevron -> confirmExit() (L276-287, confirm dialog + wipe). StudyStack sets gestureEnabled:false (StudyStack.tsx L32) which blocks only the iOS swipe gesture, not the Android hardware back button, and no BackHandler is registered anywhere in the quiz screen.
why: On Android the hardware back pops the StudyStack and exits the quiz immediately with no confirmation, bypassing the intended 'Leave quiz?' guard. The learner drops out of an in-progress timed attempt on an accidental tap (attempt resumes server-side on re-entry, but the confirm-on-exit safeguard the design relies on does not fire).
suggested_fix: Register a BackHandler (or navigation beforeRemove listener) while the attempt is live that routes hardware back through confirmExit(), matching the chevron behavior.

what: No skip/next fallback for an unanswerable question. If a served question has empty/malformed options, no selectable control renders and there is no way to advance: single (mc/fill) -> singleOpts=[] (L336) renders zero AnswerCells; multi_select -> Confirm stays disabled while multiSel.size===0 (L395); matching with empty lefts -> k===0 so recordAndAdvance is never reached (L269-271). The render guards (L328-336) deliberately trade a crash for an empty screen, but leave no forward path.
why: A single bad question payload blocks the entire linear quiz — the learner is stuck on that slot with no answer control and no next button until the 10-minute deadline force-submits (doSubmit at L172-175), effectively failing/timing-out an otherwise capable learner.
suggested_fix: When a question renders no answerable control, surface a 'Skip / Next' affordance that records an empty answer for that slot and calls advance(), so one malformed slot cannot trap the whole attempt.

what: route.params.achievementId is read as presetTopicId (line 863) and only seeds selTopicId (line 1186); filter stays 'all' (line 919). The visible memo applies the topic narrowing only when `filter === 'topic' && selTopicId` (line 1443), so a Dashboard entry that preselects a topic never actually filters to it.
why: The screen's own header docs (lines 8-10) and navigation/types.ts ('opened from a Dashboard') promise the topic is preselected, but the preselect is dead code: opening the Glossary from a topic shows all ~3,300 terms with the 'Topic' chip un-checked, giving no indication the intended topic was ever selected.
suggested_fix: When presetTopicId is present, also initialize filter to 'topic' (useState('topic')) or run a mount effect that sets filter='topic' when selTopicId is set, so the preselected topic's terms are shown.

what: The corpus loader in the focus effect (lines 1207-1241) catches load failure with only console.warn and setLoading(false); entries stays []. With entries empty the FlatList ListEmptyComponent renders 'No results for {All}' (lines 1908-1910) and the header count reads '0 Terms'.
why: A network/permission failure on first open makes the entire glossary look genuinely empty ('No results for All', 0 Terms) with no error message, spinner, or retry affordance. The user cannot tell the load failed and has no in-screen way to retry (only leaving and re-focusing the tab re-fetches, since a failed load is not session-cached).
suggested_fix: Track a load-error state in the catch and render a distinct 'Couldn't load the glossary — check your connection' message with a Retry button (re-invoke loadAllEntries), instead of falling through to the empty-results copy.

what: The "SET UP MY PROFILE ›" button (line ~204-215) whose onPress does `hasAccount ? navigate('AudioCommunityDirectory') : setAcctNote(true)` is rendered ONLY inside the `!hasAccount` branch (registryBox). So hasAccount is always false when the button exists and the navigate('AudioCommunityDirectory') branch is unreachable dead code. Registered users get the `registryBoxCol` branch (QR only), which has NO button into the Audio Community Directory.
why: On this 'Get Discovered' page a signed-in account holder has no control to reach the community directory / profile editor; the intended navigation never fires. Guests only ever get the account-required prompt. The CTA is effectively broken for its target audience.
suggested_fix: Render a working CTA in the registered (registryBoxCol) branch that calls navigation.navigate('AudioCommunityDirectory'), and drop the always-false ternary in the guest button (guest branch can just call setAcctNote(true)).

what: fetchPublicProfile(token) resolves to null on any error/not-found (its catch returns null; it never rejects). The effect (line ~100-117) does setData(d); setBusy(false) with no null/error handling, and the render guard is `busy || !p ? <Loading label='Loading profile…'/>`. When data is null, busy is false but p is undefined, so the sheet shows the 'Loading profile…' spinner forever. The local `err` state is never set from the load.
why: A network failure, a deleted profile, or a blocked member produces a permanent fake 'Loading…' with no error message and no retry — the user cannot tell the load failed.
suggested_fix: Track a loaded-but-null case: after the fetch, if d is null set an error/empty state (e.g. 'This profile could not be loaded' + a retry/close) instead of leaving p undefined under the busy||!p guard.

what: Failed Login and Create Account surface the raw Supabase error.message: signIn() returns error.message verbatim (api.ts line 77) and ensureSession() returns the raw error.message (line 72) which AuthScreen.onLogin/onCreateAccount push straight into setError. The friendly REGISTER_ERROR_COPY map (api.ts lines 36-41) is not applied to this path.
why: On a bad password / auth failure the user is shown a technical backend string rather than mapped, human-readable copy, so the error readout is inconsistent and can be opaque.
suggested_fix: Map auth errors to friendly copy (invalid-credentials -> 'Email or password is incorrect') before setError, instead of relaying error.message.

what: onLogin routes via toMain = navigation.reset({index:0,routes:[{name:'Main'}]}) with no nested screen param; MainTabs sets initialRouteName='Home' (Course Selection), so login lands on Home -- identical to onCreateAccount's toHome (Main/Home). The inline comment on line 241 claims 'Study tab = Dashboard'.
why: The comment contradicts actual behavior (lands on Home, not Study/Dashboard). No dead-end (Home is a real screen), but the misleading comment invites a future wrong 'fix' and signals the intended post-login landing was never wired.
suggested_fix: Either route login to Main/Study to match the comment, or correct the comment to 'lands on Home (Course Selection)'.

what: The 'firstUserWelcome' intro ('First-Time Walkthrough' / guided first-run tour) is defined in SCREEN_INTROS (screenIntros.ts lines 71-75) and in the IntroKey union, but grep shows it is never rendered by any ScreenIntroOverlay/useScreenIntro/ScreenIntroSequence call anywhere in the app.
why: The promised first-run guided tour onboarding step has no trigger, so a brand-new user never sees it -- a defined onboarding sequence step that is unreachable.
suggested_fix: Wire firstUserWelcome into the first entry (e.g. via ScreenIntroSequence after appWelcome) or remove the dead registry entry.

what: The appWelcome copy shown over AuthScreen promises 'Browse our professional audio glossary immediately-no account required' (screenIntros.ts lines 52-53), but AuthScreen exposes only Create Account / Login / Guest Mode buttons -- no glossary-browse control. The dedicated PublicGlossary route is navigated to ONLY from features/dev/DevVisualIndex.tsx (no production entry point).
why: The landing copy invites a direct no-account glossary browse that has no matching navigation control on the screen; the anonymous glossary is only reachable indirectly by entering full Guest Mode, so displayed copy and available navigation disagree.
suggested_fix: Add a 'Browse glossary' action on AuthScreen that navigates to PublicGlossary, or adjust the welcome copy to point at Guest Mode.

what: In mode==='recovery' the Email TextField remains mounted and editable (it is rendered above the mode branch, lines 353-359), while onSubmitNewPassword calls verifyRecoveryOtp(email.trim(), resetCode) using the live email value.
why: If the user edits the email after the 6-digit code was emailed to the original address, verifyRecoveryOtp fails and the UI shows the generic 'That code is incorrect or expired' message (line 290) -- a misleading readout that blames the code rather than the changed email.
suggested_fix: Lock/disable the email field once mode switches to 'recovery', or validate that email is unchanged before verifying.

what: The top-right RETURN button (navigation.goBack(), lines 321-331) is rendered whenever navigation.canGoBack(), including while mode==='recovery'. It is not suppressed during the in-app password-reset flow.
why: A user mid-recovery (code already emailed, entering new password) can tap RETURN and be navigated away with no confirmation, abandoning the reset with the emailed code unused; only the Cancel button is intended to exit recovery.
suggested_fix: Hide the RETURN button when mode==='recovery' (render it only in main mode) so recovery is exited only via Cancel.

what: navProxy intercepts navigate('Dashboard') and remaps it to target.goBack() (lines 24-31), on the assumption there is always a screen to return to. PublicGlossary is a root-stack screen; if it is ever presented as the entry/first route (no back history), goBack() is a no-op.
why: When there is no back history, the reused GlossaryScreen's mode icon (which fires navigate('Dashboard')) becomes a dead control -- the user taps it and nothing happens, with no alternate exit. Currently low-risk because the only wired entry is the dev index, but the shell has no guard.
suggested_fix: In the proxy, fall back to a concrete route (e.g. reset to Auth/Main) when navigation.canGoBack() is false, instead of an unconditional goBack().

what: On the single-device takeover 'Continue' path, claimAndProceed does `void claimThisDevice().then(proceed)` (lines 100-102) with no .catch and busy already reset to false (line 86).
why: If claimThisDevice() rejects, proceed() (the navigation.reset into Home/Main) never runs and no error is surfaced, leaving the user on the Auth screen with no feedback after they confirmed taking over the device.
suggested_fix: Add a .catch to claimThisDevice().then(proceed) that surfaces an error (setError) and/or still proceeds, so a failed claim is not a silent no-op.

what: fetchEarnedCredentialsByType(kind).then(setRows).catch(() => setRows([])) collapses an error into an empty list, so a failed read renders as '0 EARNED' + the waiting slot exactly like a genuinely-empty account. Separately fetchNearestCredential(...).catch(() => setNearest(null)) leaves nearest null on error, and the null branch of WaitingSlot renders the 'Finding your next {noun}…' loading placeholder permanently.
why: On a read failure the earned Certificates/Programs list silently claims zero earned (could hide credentials the user actually holds), and the top waiting slot shows a perpetual 'Finding your next…' spinner instead of an error.
suggested_fix: Distinguish error from empty for both reads; show a brief 'Couldn’t load — pull to retry' row rather than an implied-empty list or a stuck loading slot.

what: fetchTopicAchievements().catch(() => setFields([])) and a genuinely-empty v3 curriculum both produce subjects=[] which renders only the 'SUBJECTS' header with no rows and a '0 / 0' counter; there is no empty-state copy and no error copy (unlike GalleryScreen which has an explicit empty line).
why: Pre-launch (no curriculum published yet) or a fetch error shows a bare header over blank space with no explanation, reading as a broken screen.
suggested_fix: When subjects.length === 0, render an empty/error message (e.g. 'No topics available yet' vs 'Couldn’t load topics — pull to retry'), tracking error separately from the loaded-empty case.

what: Every gallery entry comes from fetchGalleryV3 (filtered to status='complete', i.e. earned trophies), yet the onPress navigates to 'Trophy' with badgeEarned: false hardcoded. The earned/awarded flag passed to the Trophy route is the opposite of the entry's actual earned state.
why: The load-bearing badgeEarned param tells the Trophy screen the trophy is NOT earned for items that are, by this list's own query, all earned — risking a 'not yet earned' presentation when opening an earned trophy from the gallery.
suggested_fix: Pass badgeEarned: true for gallery entries (all are earned), or derive it from the entry, rather than a fixed false.

what: The static TierBlock co-requisite list (awardsData SPECIALIZATION/PROGRAM tiers) shows 3 co-reqs — 'Pro Audio Safety','Grounding & Electrical','Workplace Skills' — while the picker's REQUIRED CORE banner renders 4 from COREQ_TOPIC_GS [3060,3070,3081,4370] (adds Audio Fundamentals Lab gs3081). The tier also labels gs3070 'Grounding & Electrical' whereas the gs3070 topic name is 'Grounding & Shielding'.
why: The co-requisite readout disagrees between the tier page and the enrollment picker (3 vs 4 items) and uses a non-matching name for gs3070, so the same requirement set is presented two different ways on adjacent surfaces.
suggested_fix: Drive the tier co-req list from COREQ_TOPIC_GS (resolved via nameForGs) so it matches the picker banner exactly, including the correct gs3070 name.

what: Program picker card meta computes total = COREQ_TOPIC_GS.length + p.requiredTopics.length (p.requiredTopics = v3 topicsGs). This is a client-side approximation of the server's award_required_topics union; if program_topics ever overlaps the standing requirements, or the server rule differs, this preview count will not match the AwardProgress screen's totalCount. The certificate picker sub-copy is also fixed ('plus 3 specialization topics') while c.specializationTopics length is dynamic.
why: The 'N required topics' figure shown in the picker can disagree with the authoritative totalCount rendered on AwardProgress for the same award, and the '3 specialization topics' copy is stale for any v3 certificate whose topicsGs length ≠ 3.
suggested_fix: Prefer the server award_required_topics count for the total (or clearly label the picker number as an estimate), and make the certificate sub-copy count from specializationTopics.length rather than a hardcoded 3.

what: The earned-row TrophyModal always renders action {label:'DOWNLOAD CERTIFICATE'} and calls exportCertificate without first checking certificatePdf.isAvailable(). AwardProgressScreen gates the identical control behind certificateExportAvailable() and shows an honest note when the native print/share modules aren't in the build.
why: In a build lacking the expo-print/expo-sharing native halves, the modal still presents a Download button that can do nothing but surface a 'needs the next app build' message on tap — an inconsistent, misleading affordance versus the gated AwardProgress screen.
suggested_fix: Import isAvailable from certificatePdf and only render the download action when it returns true, otherwise show the same 'needs the next app build' note used on AwardProgressScreen.

what: When totalCount === 0 and not earned, the screen shows 'No requirements are published for this award yet.' AND still renders the actions block with a disabled 'Take Final Exam' plus 'Complete every required topic to unlock the Final Exam.' (allComplete is false because api sets allComplete = topics.length>0 && ...).
why: A zero-requirement award reads contradictorily: it says no requirements are published, then instructs the user to 'complete every required topic' to unlock an exam — a locked exam for an award that has nothing to complete.
suggested_fix: When totalCount === 0, suppress the Final Exam actions block (or show a distinct 'Not yet available' state) instead of the generic locked-exam gate copy.

what: fmtDate(iso: string) does new Date(iso).toLocaleDateString(...) with no NaN/invalid guard, unlike sibling screens (AwardProgress fmtDate, Topics fmtDate) which guard null/NaN. It relies entirely on the fetchGalleryV3 query filter .not('date_earned','is',null).
why: A malformed or unexpected date_earned value would render 'Invalid Date' in the card meta rather than being handled; the guard present in every sibling date formatter is missing here.
suggested_fix: Add a Number.isNaN(d.getTime()) guard returning '' (as Topics/AwardProgress do) so a bad date degrades cleanly.

what: fetchMyCredentials().then(setCredentials) (line ~175) and Promise.all([fetchV3Certs(), fetchV3Programs()]).then(...) (line ~235) have no .catch, unlike the sibling fetchProfile().catch(()=>{}) right beside them. A rejection is an unhandled promise rejection.
why: Inconsistent error handling; RN won't hard-crash but the credential list / cert-id maps silently never resolve and the rejection is logged unhandled.
suggested_fix: Add .catch(()=>{}) (or set an error state) to both credential fetches, matching fetchProfile.

what: fetchProfile().then(setProfile).catch(()=>{}) (line ~170) swallows all errors. On a transient failure for a real signed-in member, profile stays null so apeStudentId, qrToken (the ID card QR), overallPct and completeCount all blank/zero with no error indicator or retry — the ID card the user opened to be scanned shows no ID number and a pending QR.
why: Silent catch with no error UI; only recovers on next focus refetch.
suggested_fix: Track a load-error state and show a small retry/notice on the ID card and MY PROGRESS when the profile read fails, rather than rendering as if the fields are genuinely empty.

what: setWeeklyOn's push-auto-enable branch (line ~220: if(!prefs.push_enabled) updateNotificationPref('push_enabled',true)) is unreachable from the UI: the Weekly-concept Toggle is disabled={!prefs || groupLocked} and groupLocked = !push_enabled, so the switch cannot be tapped while push is off.
why: Dead code / contradiction — the design-review fix it documents can never fire because the control that would trigger it is disabled in exactly the state it targets.
suggested_fix: Either allow the Weekly-concept toggle to auto-enable push (remove groupLocked from its disabled condition and keep the auto-enable), or delete the now-unreachable branch and its comment.

what: The same entitlement is labeled differently across screens: 'free' shows as 'REFERENCE MODE' in Profile (line ~409) but 'FREE' in Settings (line ~562/567). A guest (anonymous) also shows 'REFERENCE MODE' in Profile — indistinguishable from a free member — while Settings distinguishes 'GUEST — NO ACCOUNT' from 'FREE'.
why: Two independent label ladders for the anonymous|free|academy|lapsed states; free and anonymous collapse to one string in Profile.
suggested_fix: Centralize the tier-label mapping (one helper in EntitlementProvider) and reuse it in both screens so free vs guest and the wording are consistent.

what: MY PROGRESS summary and 'Full Course Certification' show profile.overallPct unclamped (line ~561/568). fetchProfile computes overallPct = floor(completeCount/50*100) with a fixed ALBUM_DENOMINATOR of 50, so a user who completes more than 50 topics reads >100% in the text (the progress bar itself clamps via Math.min(100,...), so bar and number disagree).
why: Denominator hard-locked to 50 while completeCount is uncapped; only the bar width is clamped.
suggested_fix: Clamp the displayed percentage to 100 (Math.min(100, overallPct)) or cap completeCount at the denominator.

what: The 'Trophies & records' row is gated by caps.completionRecords (line ~620), which is false for the 'free' tier, yet free has caps.albumAchievements=true. A free user cannot reach Achievements from Profile even though the ladder grants them Album/Achievements (still reachable via the bottom Achievements tab, so not fully stranded).
why: The row keys on completionRecords rather than albumAchievements, mismatching the capability the row represents.
suggested_fix: Gate the Trophies & records row on caps.albumAchievements (or whichever cap actually governs the Achievements screen) so free members can open what they are entitled to.

what: The mount effect's promises fetchWeeklySubscriptions().then(...) and supabase.rpc('my_identity').single().then(({data})=>setApeId(...)) (lines ~120-126) have no .catch. A rejection (offline, RLS) is an unhandled promise rejection and apeId silently stays ''.
why: No error handling on these reads; inconsistent with the try/finally used for the settings/prefs load in the same effect.
suggested_fix: Add .catch handlers (leave apeId '' and/or surface a notice) to both calls.

what: A signed-in ('non-local') member whose deck loads but has zero progress shows every method LED at its floor with no rows, but there is no explicit empty/first-run affordance for a real account (the guest 'progress isn't saved' notice only renders when data.userId==='local', line ~1455). A member with an all-locked/blank topic just sees empty meters.
why: The only zero-progress messaging is guest-gated; an authenticated new user gets no 'start here' cue.
suggested_fix: Add a lightweight first-run hint for authenticated users with no method progress (or confirm the powered-off staging + START labels are considered sufficient guidance).

what: Quiz readout best_genuine_score is rendered as `${score}/${QUIZ_SIZE}` when score = topicProg?.best_genuine_score ?? '' (line ~1629). If a passed/partial row ever has a null best_genuine_score it renders '/25' (empty numerator). Guarded by ?? '' (0 is preserved correctly), so only a genuinely-null server value trips it.
why: Empty-string fallback for a numeric field produces a malformed 'x/25' readout rather than a 0 or a dash.
suggested_fix: Fall back to 0 or '—' (e.g. score ?? '—') so the score line never renders a leading empty numerator.

what: The dependency note text (line ~330-333) branches only on prefs==null vs push off. For a signed-in member whose prefs fetch failed (prefs null), it prints the guest copy 'Sign in to manage notifications — a guest session keeps nothing.' — a wrong readout for an account holder (paired consequence of the null-overload noted in the major finding).
why: prefs===null is used as a proxy for 'guest' in the copy even though it also occurs on error.
suggested_fix: Only show the guest wording when the user is actually anonymous (entitlement/isGuest), and show an error/retry message when prefs failed to load.

what: After a successful fetchConceptById, setCard(row) is rendered with no guard on empty text: the title <Text>{card.concept}</Text> (line 60) and eyebrow {card.category} (line 57) print whatever the DB row holds. hasBody() only gates the INITIAL fetch decision, not the fetched result.
why: A concept row whose `concept` column is empty (or a push whose title/category is blank) renders a blank title/eyebrow area instead of the graceful 'This concept is not available.' empty state that the null-card branch provides.
suggested_fix: Treat a fetched row with an empty `concept` as unavailable (fall through to the empty state), or render a fallback title; guard the eyebrow so an empty category/subdomain does not print a stray separator.

what: The MY ENROLLMENT sub-count renders `{activeCount} of {enrolled.length} Enrolled` (lines 1181-1183). activeCount counts topics with active=true; enrolled.length is the FULL list including completed topics, which are filtered out of the visible list and moved to the MY RECORD folder (displayed = enrolled.filter(pct<100), line 692).
why: The denominator counts rows the user cannot see in the list (completed topics live only in MY RECORD), and the label 'Enrolled' is applied to the 'active' numerator, so the header count can disagree with the number of visible cards (e.g. '3 of 5 Enrolled' while only 3 rows show).
suggested_fix: Label the numerator/denominator to match what is shown (e.g. active-of-incomplete), or compute the denominator from the same non-completed set the list renders, so the count and the visible cards agree.

what: On a stored cert/program bundle the 'TAKE FINAL EXAM' button is hard-coded `disabled` (lines 915-923), and stays disabled even when the bundle is COMPLETED (done). There is no enabled path to the award's Final Exam from this screen.
why: A completed certificate/program presents a permanently inert primary CTA with no forward action from Enrollment; the real Final Exam / AwardProgress routes exist but are not linked here, so a user who finishes an award has a visible dead button and no next step on this screen.
suggested_fix: When the bundle is complete, enable the button and route to the FinalExam/AwardProgress flow (navigation.navigate('AwardProgress', {...})), or remove the placeholder button until the exam flow is wired to it.

what: On pass, the credential box (lines 84-91) says the credential 'can be viewed from your profile', but the only navigation control is 'Done' -> navigation.goBack() (lines 98-102), which after the preceding popToTop lands on Main with no direct route to Profile.
why: The instruction to view the credential on the profile has no supporting affordance from this terminal screen; not a hard dead-end but a broken hand-off.
suggested_fix: Offer a 'View on Profile' action on pass that navigates to Main/Profile, in addition to Done.

what: In doSubmit, submitted.current is set true at the start (line 110) and is never reset. On a non-network submit failure the catch calls notify('Submit failed', ..., () => navigation.goBack()) (line 137) with no in-place retry; the double-submit guard stays latched.
why: If a submit fails for a non-network reason the user cannot resubmit from the mounted screen; recovery depends entirely on unmount + server-side resume on re-entry. A transient server error therefore reads as a lost attempt.
suggested_fix: Reset submitted.current = false in the non-network error branch so the user can retry, or add an explicit Retry action to the failure notify.

what: On the successful submit path doSubmit calls navigation.popToTop() then navigate('FinalExamResult') (lines 124-125), unmounting this screen, and the finally block still runs setSubmitting(false) (line 140) on the now-unmounted component.
why: Set-state-on-unmounted-component: harmless at runtime but emits a React warning and indicates the loading flag outlives the screen.
suggested_fix: Guard the finally with an isMounted ref, or navigate after the finally, so state is not set post-unmount.

what: questionText() calls questions.find(...) at line 65 with no runtime guard; result.wrong_answers is defensively coalesced with ?? {} (line 61) but the questions param is not.
why: If a caller navigates to Results without the questions array (undefined), the review list render throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading find)'. The param is typed required, so this is a defensive gap rather than a live path.
suggested_fix: Default the param: const questions = route.params.questions ?? []; before use.

what: The achievements fetch (lines 41-49) chains .then with no .catch; a rejected Supabase promise is unhandled. Data reads are optional-chained so a null result degrades gracefully, but a network/permission rejection has no handler.
why: An unhandled promise rejection on load; the badge/icon simply never populate with no signal. Not a crash but no error state.
suggested_fix: Add a .catch that logs and leaves the fallback ('a badge' / placeholder icon) in place.

what: The header docblock (lines 1-8) describes 'confetti 3s + haptic', but line 72 states confetti was removed per user request 2026-07-18 while the success haptic still fires (line 53).
why: Doc/code drift only; no functional defect, but the comment misdescribes the screen's behavior.
suggested_fix: Update the docblock to match: haptic only, no confetti/award animation.

what: Quiz thresholds are hardcoded in copy strings rather than derived: the clamp notice says 'Score 24+' (line 138) and the docblock encodes partial_pass 20-23 / no_pass <=19, while the score readout uses '/ {QUIZ_SIZE}' (line 129). Branching itself uses server result.outcome, so the numbers are display-only text.
why: If QUIZ_SIZE or the pass/partial thresholds change server-side, the copy ('24+') silently misstates the requirement to users; the constant and the prose can diverge.
suggested_fix: Derive the numeric thresholds from shared constants (e.g. QUIZ_SIZE-based) and interpolate them into the copy instead of literals.

what: The in-exam pass mark shown in the sub-bar is computed client-side as Math.max(1, payload.items.length - 2) (line 316; rendered 'PASS {passMark}/{items.length}' lines 337-339), whereas FinalExamResultScreen displays the server's result.pass_mark and result.size (lines 74-78). For 30 served items this yields 28/30, matching the deployed 28/30 pass mark and the api.ts 'pass mark = size - 2' contract (api.ts lines 10-12).
why: Verified correct for a 30-question payload, but the pass mark is sourced two different ways (client items.length-2 vs server pass_mark); they diverge if the served payload size is ever not 30, and the in-exam figure is not authoritative.
suggested_fix: Surface the server-authoritative pass_mark/size in the exam header too (or assert payload.size === items.length) so the pre-submit and post-submit figures cannot drift.

what: The top-of-file docstring (line 8) and the onViewableItemsChanged handler (lines 1101-1110) persist the carousel index to AsyncStorage POSITION_KEY and claim 'Carousel position persists across app restarts ... otherwise you land where you left.' But the landing effect (lines 1071-1099) drives position purely from module-level vars sessionLanded/lastCenteredId, which reset on app process restart (documented lines 116-127) and NEVER reads POSITION_KEY.
why: Behavior contradicts the documented/legacy promise: a cold start always lands on the default/Glossary card, never 'where you left', and POSITION_KEY is written every swipe but never read (dead persistence). Confusing for maintainers and a stale user-facing promise.
suggested_fix: Remove the write-only POSITION_KEY (and the stale line-8 docstring), or actually read POSITION_KEY on cold start if restart-persistence is still desired. Pick one and make code and comments agree.

what: Expanded subjects pull copy from subjectMeta(s.name) (used at lines 289 and 313); subjectMeta returns { description:'', careers:'' } for any name not in its map (subjectMeta.ts line 119). The map keys are v2-era subject names while s.name comes from the live v3 fetch, so a v3 subject whose name does not match a map key expands with no description line and no CAREER APPLICATIONS section (both are conditionally rendered on truthy strings).
why: Subjects can expand to show only the topic/terms meta line with silently missing description and career copy, giving an inconsistent, half-empty readout with no indication anything is missing.
suggested_fix: Reconcile subjectMeta keys with the live v3 subject names (or key meta by a stable subject id rather than display name), and/or show a neutral placeholder when description/careers are absent.

what: With FIELD_TOPICS=[] (line 147) and load()/buildPublicCatalog building only the lab/tools/glossary + two free-taster cards (lines 964-987), the Card kinds 'course','public','comingTopic','programStub','more' and their handlers (openCourse->Study/Dashboard, openMore->Awards specialization, openPrograms->Awards program, the paid onOpenPublic path) are currently unreachable. onOpenPrograms is passed to CourseCardView (line 1427) but never invoked by any card.
why: Large portions of card rendering and their navigation targets cannot be exercised with current data, so those nav routes are effectively untested; if catalog data ever repopulates these kinds, the deadend/route correctness is unverified. onOpenPrograms is dead wiring.
suggested_fix: Prune the unreachable card kinds/handlers, or gate their reintroduction behind tests that assert each navigate() target ('Study','Awards' with category, 'ToolsHub','AudioLearning','Paywall') resolves to a registered route. Remove the unused onOpenPrograms prop.

what: LabCategory is registered in RootNavigator (line 291) and typed (types.ts lines 178-179) as the 'second level of the Audio Learning Lab hierarchy', but nothing navigates to the 'LabCategory' route. EarLabScreen opens hubs/labs directly via go(cat.route)/go(leaf.route) from labCatalog, and no labCatalog entry has route:'LabCategory'. Only non-navigation refs exist (its own screen + an ExposureCheckin suppress-list name).
why: LabCategoryScreen is dead code from a superseded IA restructure; it can never be shown. No user trap, but it is misleading dead wiring in the backbone.
suggested_fix: Either remove the LabCategory route + screen, or reintroduce the intermediate step by having EarLab navigate('LabCategory', { id }) for hub categories instead of jumping straight to the lab.

what: Directory is registered as a modal (RootNavigator line 248). types.ts (lines 127-128) claims it is 'kept as a route ALIAS so every existing internal link and deep link still resolves', but every in-app link navigates 'AudioCommunityDirectory' instead — there is no navigate('Directory') anywhere, and no linking/deep-link configuration exists in the audited source (no NavigationContainer linking config in appsrc).
why: The aliased Directory route has no in-app entry and (absent any linking config in the audited source) no deep-link entry either, so it is effectively unreachable — a dead modal.
suggested_fix: Confirm the app-root NavigationContainer defines a linking config that maps the Directory deep link; if none exists, remove the Directory route or point its former entry points at AudioCommunityDirectory.

what: PublicGlossary is registered (RootNavigator line 372) and documented as the 'anonymous public glossary (commercial browse path)', but the only navigate('PublicGlossary') in the codebase is in src/features/dev/DevVisualIndex.tsx (a dev-only visual index). No production screen opens it.
why: The intended anonymous commercial browse path has no production entry point, so real users cannot reach it — the route is dev-only.
suggested_fix: Wire a navigate('PublicGlossary') from the landing/Auth screen (or wherever anonymous browse is offered); otherwise drop the route if the commercial browse path was cut.

what: Stale size/time constants in docs and init. The file header (L2-17) documents 'QUESTION n OF 25' and a fixed 10:00 / 602s model, while api.ts L80-83 ratifies QUIZ_SIZE=30 / QUIZ_PASS=28; msLeft initializes to a hardcoded 600_000 (L67).
why: The visible counter is actually correct because it derives from payload.questions.length (L353), and the timer recomputes from deadline on the first 250ms tick, so no wrong number is shown for long — but the 25-vs-30 doc drift and the hardcoded 10:00 init are traps for the next editor and briefly show 10:00 before the server time_limit_seconds is applied.
suggested_fix: Update the header comment to the 30/28 shape and initialize msLeft from payload.time_limit_seconds (or null-render the timer until deadline is known).

what: Start-error state offers only 'Back', no retry. On any startQuizAttempt failure (including the transient 'offline' copy) the screen renders the message plus a single Back button that calls navigation.goBack() (L290-299).
why: A transient connectivity blip on start ejects the learner all the way back to the Dashboard to re-launch the quiz, rather than letting them retry in place; quiz start is online-only so this path is hit on any brief network hiccup.
suggested_fix: Add a 'Try again' action on the start-error view that re-runs startQuizAttempt (reset startError and re-trigger the start effect) alongside Back.

what: Web offline-submit queue is in-memory only (Map, L17) with no persistence across reloads, per the file's own note (L1-7). Native uses SQLite (submissionQueueStorage.native.ts); web does not.
why: On the web build, an offline submit that gets enqueued (QuizScreen L152) is lost if the tab reloads before reconnect, so that finished attempt is never scored/replayed. Documented tradeoff, but it is a silent data-loss path for a completed quiz on web.
suggested_fix: Persist the web queue (IndexedDB/localStorage) or surface a clear 'do not close this tab until reconnected' warning when a web submission is queued offline.

what: blankOut (lines 61-68) builds its regex as new RegExp(escapedTerm, 'gi') with NO word boundaries, then splits the sentence on every match.
why: A short term that is a substring of other words (e.g. 'bus', 'amp') is blanked mid-word, producing corrupted prompts like 'com______tion' for 'combustion'. The matching path uses boundary-aware termLeakPatterns, but FIB does not.
suggested_fix: Add word boundaries to the blanking regex (or reuse leakPatternsV2/maskLeaks from features/study/sentences.ts) so only whole-word occurrences of the term are blanked.

what: Both screens auto-advance after every answer/board and wrap with modulo (FIB setQIdx(i+1) at line 297; Matching goBoardRef advance at lines 328-329 with (i+dir+len)%len at line 268). There is no guard that stops auto-advance once displayPct reaches 100%.
why: The locked-behavior headers of both files state '100% → manual back only', i.e. auto-advance should stop at completion. Instead the deck keeps cycling answered items indefinitely, contradicting the documented spec (harmless re-practice, but not the specified stop).
suggested_fix: When studyDisplayPct >= 100, suppress the auto-advance timer/board-complete advance and require Prev/Next (or RETURN), per the documented behavior.

what: A topic that loads with zero items leaves items=[] (so the `if (!items)` spinner guard at line 1152 is skipped) and deck=[]; the card area renders the generic 'No cards match / Adjust the filter buttons above to see cards' placeholder (lines 1446-1450).
why: For a genuinely empty topic there are no filters to adjust, so the message misleads. FillInBlankScreen and MatchingScreen show a correct 'This topic has no … items yet.' empty state; Flashcards has no equivalent distinct empty-topic message.
suggested_fix: Add an items.length===0 branch (mirroring FIB/Matching) that shows 'This topic has no flashcards yet.' with a Back control, distinct from the filter-hidden 'No cards match' state.

what: levelText() level 5 returns join(item.common_mistakes) ?? item.definition (line 161). fetchTopicItems leaves common_mistakes null for non-academy users, so the MISTAKES section silently falls back to showing the plain definition text under the 'MISTAKES' eyebrow (label from LEVEL_LABELS[4]).
why: The card shows the definition again beneath a 'MISTAKES' heading — a mislabeled duplicate. GlossaryScreen instead veils Common Mistakes with a lock/upgrade CTA for the same non-member case, so the two surfaces are inconsistent.
suggested_fix: When common_mistakes is null, render an explicit empty/locked treatment for the MISTAKES level (e.g. a members-only note) rather than falling back to the definition under the MISTAKES label.

what: fetchDetails (lines 1033-1060) does base `glossary` select().single(); on `if (!data) return;` it never populates details[id], so the expanded row/popup stays on the 'Loading…' text (lines 2126, 2268) if the base fetch fails.
why: A transient failure of the detail fetch leaves the term stuck showing 'Loading…' with no error or retry shown. It is recoverable only by collapsing and re-expanding (which re-calls fetchDetails since details[id] is still undefined), which the user isn't told.
suggested_fix: On a failed/empty detail fetch, set an error marker for that id and render a short 'Couldn't load details — tap to retry' in place of the perpetual 'Loading…'.

what: There is no deep-link/linking configuration anywhere in the app (no LinkingOptions/prefixes/getStateFromPath), and the Glossary route params (navigation/types.ts) accept only {achievementId?, topicName?} — no term id. A term can be reached only by in-app browse/search/cross-link (openPopupRoot/openLinked), never by a term-targeted route or URL.
why: The audit item 'deep link to a term resolves' has no supporting mechanism: neither an external URL nor an internal navigate() can target a specific glossary term, only the topic preselect (which itself is broken — see separate finding).
suggested_fix: If term deep-linking is required, add a term/termId param to the Glossary route (and a linking config) and have the screen call openPopupRoot(termId) on mount when present; otherwise document that term deep-linking is intentionally unsupported.

what: question.options is built as shuffle([term, ...distractors]) where distractors = shuffle(order without item).map(term).slice(0,3) (lines 239-241). For a topic with fewer than 4 items the grid shows fewer than 4 options, and a 1-item topic shows only the single correct answer.
why: On very small topics the 2x2 answer grid degrades to 1-3 cells (a 1-item topic guarantees the correct answer), a weak/confusing question. No crash, but the '4-option grid' locked behavior is not met for tiny topics.
suggested_fix: Guard tiny topics (e.g. require a minimum item count for FIB, or pad distractors from a broader pool) so a real multi-option question is always shown, or route tiny topics away from FIB.

what: load() calls fetchContactThreads(), which swallows errors and returns [] (api.ts line ~380-398). A genuine load failure therefore sets threads=[] and renders the EmptyState 'No contact requests yet', identical to truly having none. The `err` banner is only wired to act()/block, not to the initial load. ThreadSheet.fetchThreadMessages has the same swallow-to-[] behavior.
why: A user whose requests fail to load is told they have none, hiding pending incoming contact requests and masking connectivity problems.
suggested_fix: Have fetchContactThreads surface an error (or return a discriminated outcome) so RequestsView can show a warn banner + retry instead of the empty state when the fetch fails.

what: label(kind, slug) falls back to the raw slug when the slug is absent from the fetched taxonomy: `tax?.[kind].find(x=>x.slug===slug)?.label ?? slug` (line ~113-116). Chosen specialties/roles/areas render through this (e.g. line 318, and the PreviewSheet), so on taxonomy drift (a removed/renamed slug still stored on the profile) the chip and the public-preview show a raw slug like 'foh-mixing' instead of a human label.
why: Raw ids/slugs can surface in the member's own profile chips and in the 'THIS IS WHAT OTHERS SEE' preview, which is a broken readout of what will be published.
suggested_fix: When a slug has no taxonomy label, either hide it or show a neutral 'Unavailable' rather than the raw slug, and consider dropping unknown slugs from the saved set.

what: After blockMember succeeds in MemberSheet, onClose is called but the Explore results list is not re-queried. searchDirectory runs only on filter/query change (ExploreView useEffect on [f]).
why: A member the user just blocked stays visible in the Explore list (and re-openable) until the next search, which contradicts the 'neither party sees the other' block model until a manual re-search.
suggested_fix: Trigger a re-run of the current search (run(f)) after a successful block/report, or remove the blocked card from `rows` locally.

what: OPEN TOOL button navigates via `(navigation as any).navigate(OPEN_TOOL_ROUTE[tool.key])` (line ~129). The `as any` cast bypasses route-name type checking; the button is correctly hidden for keys absent from OPEN_TOOL_ROUTE, so today it is safe, but any future OPEN_TOOL_ROUTE entry pointing at a route not registered in RootNavigator would navigate to a non-existent screen with no compile-time guard.
why: The type cast removes the safety net that would otherwise catch a bad/renamed route name; a typo would become a runtime nav failure rather than a build error.
suggested_fix: Type OPEN_TOOL_ROUTE values as keyof RootStackParamList (already done) and navigate without the `as any`, or add a dev assert that the target route exists before navigating.
